events.title: Execution of Marie Antoinette
events.description: Former Queen of France Marie Antoinette was guillotined in the Place de la Révolution in Paris after being convicted of treason by the Revolutionary Tribunal during the French Revolution.
events.significance: Her execution symbolized the radical phase of the French Revolution and the definitive end of the Bourbon monarchy's authority during the Reign of Terror.

events.title: First Public Demonstration of Ether Anesthesia
events.description: At Massachusetts General Hospital in Boston, dentist William T.G. Morton demonstrated the use of ether as a surgical anesthetic while surgeon John Collins Warren removed a tumor from patient Gilbert Abbott.
events.significance: This demonstration, held in what became known as the Ether Dome, revolutionized surgery by allowing painless, longer, and more complex operations, and spread rapidly around the world.

events.title: Walt Disney Cartoon Studio Founded
events.description: Walt Disney and his brother Roy O. Disney founded the Disney Brothers Cartoon Studio in Los Angeles after Walt signed a contract to produce the Alice Comedies series.
events.significance: The small studio grew into The Walt Disney Company, one of the largest and most influential entertainment conglomerates in the world.

events.title: Cuban Missile Crisis Begins for US Leadership
events.description: President John F. Kennedy was shown photographic evidence from U-2 reconnaissance flights of Soviet nuclear missile sites under construction in Cuba, beginning the thirteen-day crisis.
events.significance: The confrontation brought the United States and Soviet Union to the brink of nuclear war and led to lasting changes in Cold War diplomacy, including the establishment of the Moscow-Washington hotline.

events.title: Karol Wojtyła Elected Pope John Paul II
events.description: Cardinal Karol Wojtyła of Poland was elected pope by the papal conclave, taking the name John Paul II and becoming the first non-Italian pope in 455 years.
events.significance: His long pontificate played a major role in the fall of communism in Eastern Europe, transformed the modern papacy through extensive international travel, and shaped the Catholic Church for decades.
